games.title: Vampire Slayer
games.note: Cult-beloved GoldSrc Half-Life multiplayer mod (often remembered as 'Vampire Hunters') pitting human Slayers—huddling inside creaking gothic mansions with pump and double-barreled shotguns, crossbows, and wooden stakes—against nocturnal Vampires bounding silently across moonlit rooftops, turning invisible in shadows, and regenerating unless staked through the heart while downed.

games.title: The Hidden: Source
games.note: Terrifying 1-vs-8 asymmetric Source-engine mod where one nearly invisible, wall-clinging experiment (Subject 617) armed with a combat knife, pipe bombs, and whispered voice taunts stalks a panicked IRIS SWAT squad sweeping dark corridors.

games.title: The Specialists
games.dev: Filippo De Luca & Lorenzo Pasqui (Half-Life Mod)
games.note: Turned Half-Life multiplayer into The Matrix meets John Woo: multiplayer slow-motion bullet-time bubbles, wall-flips, Max Payne dives through lobby glass, kung-fu weapon disarms, katanas, and dual-wielded Colts.

games.title: Science and Industry
games.note: Deadpan corporate-espionage Half-Life mod where rival megacorporations raid each other's offices to club and kidnap labcoat scientists over their shoulders—because whichever team holds more scientists researches bizarre prototype weapons faster.

games.title: Natural Selection
games.note: Fused real-time strategy with claustrophobic FPS horror inside Half-Life: one Marine sat in a top-down RTS Command Chair welding doors and dropping ammo while teammates crept down dark vents hunted by ceiling-crawling Skulk aliens—launching Unknown Worlds (later creators of Subnautica).

games.title: Sven Co-op
games.dev: Daniel 'Sven Viking' Fearon & Sven Co-op Team
games.note: Launched just two months after Half-Life so LAN friends could play the entire Black Mesa campaign and hundreds of chaotic community puzzle and boss maps cooperatively—eventually gifted standalone GoldSrc engine rights by Valve.

games.title: They Hunger
games.dev: Neil Manke / Black Widow Games (Half-Life Mod)
games.note: Three-episode George A. Romero-style zombie horror total conversion distributed free on PC Gamer cover discs, turning Half-Life into foggy country churches, undead sheriffs, and asylum escapes years before Resident Evil 4.

games.title: Cry of Fear
games.note: Built over four years by young Swedish modder Andreas Rönnberg and Team Psykskallar, pushing 1998 GoldSrc to psychological survival-horror limits across dark, rain-slicked Stockholm streets illuminated only by a flip-phone screen.

games.title: Desert Combat (Battlefield 1942 Mod)
games.note: Overhauled DICE's WWII Battlefield 1942 into modern combined-arms warfare with M1A1 Abrams tanks, A-10 Warthogs, and famously high-skill AH-6 Little Bird helicopters—so popular that DICE acquired Trauma Studios to help build Battlefield 2.

games.title: Threewave Capture the Flag (Quake Mod)
games.note: Coded over a weekend for Quake, inventing symmetric red-vs-blue Capture the Flag bases, Tech runes, and the frantic off-hand grappling hook—leading Valve to hire Zoid and Retro Studios to recruit him onto Metroid Prime.

games.title: Trouble in Terrorist Town (TTT)
games.note: Built inside Garry's Mod using Counter-Strike: Source assets, turning firefights into hilarious voice-chat social deduction—Innocents, hidden Traitors, and a Detective with a DNA scanner—nine years before Among Us went global.

games.title: Prop Hunt
games.note: Turned Source physics props into pure multiplayer slapstick: one team disguised themselves as coffee mugs, traffic cones, and office chairs while Hunters took damage every time they shot an innocent trash can—later adopted into Call of Duty and Fortnite.

games.title: Black Mesa
games.note: Started in 2004 by over 40 volunteer modders determined to rebuild Half-Life inside Source with a completely reimagined Xen alien world—eventually blessed by Valve for a full commercial release after 16 years of craft.

games.title: XCOM: Long War
games.note: Expanded XCOM: Enemy Unknown into a grueling 120-hour global guerrilla campaign with eight soldier classes, fatigue rosters, and strategic alien research—so revered that Firaxis lead designer Jake Solomon called his own game 'basically a 20-hour tutorial for Long War.'
